bug_semantics: The public storefront GraphQL order query accepts a caller-controlled order UUID and loads the matching order without authenticating the caller or constraining the query to the current customer or guest session. A remote unauthenticated caller who obtains a valid UUID can therefore read another customer's order and nested PII-bearing fields such as customer identity, billing/shipping addresses, purchased items, totals, payment status, and shipment data.
flaw_origin: Commit 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e is the smallest true first-writer of the authorization flaw. In packages/core/src/modules/checkout/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js it removed tokenPayload-derived customerId/sid ownership predicates from Query.order and replaced the protected order_id lookup with only query.where('uuid', '=', id). The original resolver commit 44a884b59e51d29f5022aa5b482b6c12e56ebfaa was protected, and immediate parent b398f43d4d2eedf39abf9e3658820941cbd4babd still contains that protection. Later commit 52db55816458c657a7ed49dfb27daf9f280e2169 merely removed the now-unused tokenPayload parameter, and 72d478a748e7994b46f7aecee9a849a9ef15db43 renamed the public schema argument from id to uuid; neither is the BIC.
ai_marker: Absent on BIC 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e. `git cat-file commit` shows author and committer `The Nguyen <6950941+treoden@users.noreply.github.com>`, the single subject `Authentication and setting module`, and no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: Advisory and attack path: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-c73g-mx2w-cc93 identifies CVE-2025-12919, @evershop/evershop <=2.1.0, and `Patched versions: None`; https://github.com/ictrun/Evershop-Order-leak/blob/main/README.md gives an unauthenticated GraphQL request using order(uuid: $uuid) and enumerates the returned order PII. In the clone, packages/evershop/src/modules/graphql/api/graphql/route.json declares GET/POST `/graphql` with `access: public`; Order.graphql declares `order(uuid: String!): Order`; and Order.resolvers.js builds getOrdersBaseQuery(), applies only `where('uuid', '=', uuid)`, loads it, and returns camelCase(order), without consulting request identity or the tracking-token status. BIC: from the clone run `git log --all --follow -S"query.where('uuid'" -p -- packages/evershop/src/modules/oms/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js`; it identifies only 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e for first insertion. `git log -L 8,18:packages/core/src/modules/checkout/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e` traces the protected origin through 44a884b59e51d29f5022aa5b482b6c12e56ebfaa and the authorization-removing change at 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e. Parent absence: `git diff b398f43d4d2eedf39abf9e3658820941cbd4babd 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e -- packages/core/src/modules/checkout/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js` shows deletion of `const { customerId, sid } = tokenPayload`, `where('order_id', '=', id)`, `andWhere('customer_id', '=', customerId)`, and `or('sid', '=', sid)`, replaced by the UUID-only predicate. Merge shape: 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e has one parent and is a preserved member of PR #130; `git show --no-patch --format=raw c6022cedb0a86f4af2c394b2af9aa804177a0f8e` shows a two-parent merge, so there is no squash aggregate to decompose. Versions/fix: `git tag --contains 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e --sort=version:refname` lists every available release tag from 1.0.0-rc.9 through v2.2.1. `git show 1.0.0-rc.9:packages/evershop/src/modules/oms/graphql/types/Order/Order.resolvers.js` and the same command at v2.2.1 both show the UUID-only lookup with no ownership condition. Thus the advisory's <=2.1.0 range is stale relative to later tags: v2.1.1, v2.1.2, and v2.2.1 remain vulnerable. HEAD ac7a6e66f4017a0386e59a2550511e98c85ce6f0 also retains the same resolver, and full-ref `git log --all --follow -S'tokenPayload' -p -- .../Order.resolvers.js` shows the protection removed at the BIC and never restored. Marker: `git cat-file commit 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e` reproduces the human identity and marker absence.
reasoning: The vulnerability is an authorization regression, not the initial existence of an order lookup: the first implementation required the requested order to match either tokenPayload.customerId or tokenPayload.sid, while 685f3baf290024133c45986100fc7296ee14c85e deleted both constraints and made UUID existence the sole condition. The immediate parent directly proves absence, -S and -L converge on the same smallest first-writer, later argument renames and refactors preserve the mechanism, and the commit is a preserved PR member rather than a squash merge. Upstream has not closed the flaw: the newest available release tag and clone HEAD still expose it, so both fix fields are null. Under the required BIC-commit-object-only AI rule, the BIC has a human author/committer and no explicit AI attribution or bot marker; therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
remaining_gap: Unpatched upstream as of clone HEAD ac7a6e66f4017a0386e59a2550511e98c85ce6f0 and latest available release tag v2.2.1 (abfdabcacfc49ad0df1f262c34bc46af721f2537); consequently no fix commit or direct fix commit exists to record. This is an unpatched boundary, not an unresolved causal or AI-evidence gap.
